- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model underestimates the continuation of the trend (overshoot followed by underreaction).
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model too quickly brings prices back to historical averages after spikes.
- Forecasts for the last 5–10 days are often too low, suggesting underestimation of late-period volatility or policy impact.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — underestimates downward corrections.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is above 75.00.
